title: 1871: Court House, Sherman House and Chamber of Commerce match their photographs
items: The Court House's wings are rebuilt to their 1868 plan and the photograph: taller, with crested centre pavilions, urns along the parapets, and a domed pavilion on the Clark Street front.
Its great cupola has the fire watch's gallery and clock, with the open belfry and small domed cupola beside it and the north steps where the picture shows them.
Court House Square is an open lawn behind its iron fence, with no ordinary blocks standing in it.
The Sherman House's iron galleries are now open railings, with its third-floor balcony on Randolph Street, a heavier Clark Street portico and the stone balustrade round its rooftop belvedere.
The Chamber of Commerce gains the stone balcony over its three-arched entrance and the large curved pediments over its upper windows.
The balconies of the Tremont House, Crosby's Opera House and the Palmer House are open iron railings too.
